question: Should OpenClaw add a core startup-loaded immutable operator policy layer that can override mutable config and reject writes that would weaken locked values?
rationale: This changes the security boundary, config precedence, and operator recovery model; code inspection shows current Policy features are audit/conformance-only and the issue is protected maintainer-owned work.

options.title: Design the core immutable layer
options.body: Sponsor a focused design and implementation for startup loading, precedence, read-only visibility, and write rejection before any fix PR is queued.

options.title: Keep policy audit-only
options.body: Decide that policy.jsonc plus policy compare/check remains the supported enterprise baseline and explicitly decline runtime immutability for now.

options.title: Split prerequisite hook work
options.body: Defer the immutable layer until adjacent plugin hook/provenance proposals provide enough enforcement context for a narrower design.

recommendation.title: Design the core immutable layer
recommendation.body: Sponsor a focused design and implementation for startup loading, precedence, read-only visibility, and write rejection before any fix PR is queued.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc owns this issue and authored the prior exact implementation candidate, making them the clearest available decision owner for the security boundary.
